current_text: A Drake built like a barracks door, spear worn smooth from use, standing at ease the way only dangerous people stand. He watches the road and everyone on it. Including you, now.
You get your fingers into the crack; the air coming out of it is colder than the ground. Behind it the stone is dressed and set close, and nothing moves.
You can see clear along the boulder line from here. The patrol does not use it until dark.
Two of them working the inside of the boulder line, one behind the other, well after dark. Their weapons are wrapped and nothing they carry makes a sound.
[Beast's Mending] — You splint the leg and work salve into the swelling, and the joint takes weight when you press on it.
[Beast's Mending] — The splint comes off and the leg holds without it. It is up and moving before you have gathered your kit.
It is standing when you come up, weight on all four legs. You get one hand down the leg before it swings away from you and takes the rise at a trot.
A hollow pressed into the grass the length of a deer, flat and yellowed at the center. The blades around the rim have come back up already.
The pup smells your hand for a long moment, then puts its whole weight against your shin and stays there.
It walks up your arm and sets itself on your shoulder, facing back the way you came.
The hackles come up and the tussock stays between you. You have not got the hands for a wild thing yet; that comes of tending ones that are hurt.
It gets its legs under it on the second try and comes as far as your boot before it sits down hard.
You crouch down beside the scrape and it does not lift its head. Put the offer to it where it lies; it is not going to come up to meet you.
You go in sideways and shoulder-first between the two stones. The grass closes over the top of you as you come down.
The verge of the wagon road is churned where two of them are working it over, wings folded flat, long after dark. The carter fires are in sight from where they stand.
You have had the line in once today. The water has gone flat over the drop and will not give you anything else before tomorrow.

Something square and worked sits on the pond floor under a coat of silt, a stride out from the bank. The strip of water between it and the bank is a hand deep and dead still, and where the bank shades it the surface has already gone to a skin of ice.
At the top of the hollow there is one flat stone, a patch of its surface rubbed smooth. The cut in the turf runs straight up to it, and the ground on all sides of it is bare.

The yoke leaning on the basket stack was cut for goblin shoulders and stands about waist-high on you. The baskets are dark with water to the rim, and bits of cut brush are still snagged in the top one's weave.
Every basket is out and the yoke is lying on the ground. There is nothing to haul here until you have slept.
A rack of split poles over a bed of cold ash, nothing hanging on it. The hunters stand at the north lip of the hollow with the range in sight above them.
You put a hand on the rack and the old one signs at you: baskets first, then a corusdeer down off the range north. The poles stay bare until both are done.
You bring the carcass down to the poles, and the old one pinches finger and thumb nearly shut to show you the thickness. Hanging all of it takes until the light goes.
Cold spray off the basin catches the back of your hand. The face of the statue is worn soft where the water comes down on it.
